newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemenis begin voting in parliamentary elections.
newsitem.headline: Yemenis begin voting in parliamentary elections.

text.p: Yemenis began voting on Sunday in parliamentary elections seen as a test of whether the poor Arab country can guarantee the political stability needed to attract foreign investment.

As military police stood guard, polling booths opened at 8.00 a.m. (0500 GMT) and election officials began distributing ballots to voters, who included the elderly and women in black veils. Many said they had been waiting for an hour to be among the first to cast their ballot.
International and local election observers were on hand and one monitor said procedures appeared to be going well so far. Voting is scheduled to end at 6.00 p.m. (1500 GMT).

The electorate of about 4.6 million are choosing among 2,306 candidates, including 17 women, who are standing for the 301 seats under the banner of 12 parties or as independents in the first parliamentary polls since a civil war in 1994.
Diplomats expect President Ali Abdullah Saleh's ruling General People's Congress and its junior coalition partner, the Islamist Islah Party, to win a majority.
The main opposition Yemen Socialist Party and three others are boycotting the polls due to alleged irregularities. The government has denied the accusations.
